transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand before the golden threshold shaking like a dry leaf in a storm. Do you believe trembling will move the hinges, little thing? Speak quickly before I decide the floor would look better with you spread across it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to get my brother Omar back. Is that gold real on the doors?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Gold is dirt down here, as common and useless as the dust on your sandals. You crawled all the way to this gate for a boy who insulted the Well? He is likely already forgetting his own name.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He didn't mean it. He was just showing off. Do you have to stand here all the time?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Time does not flow here like water in your desert streams. I stand until I choose to sit. Why waste your final breaths asking about my habits when your life is measured in heartbeats?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was just wondering if your feet get tired. The floor looks pretty hard.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Exhaustion is a weakness of flesh that rots. Limbs forged in smokeless fire do not complain about stone. You are a strange creature to worry about the comfort of the thing that might eat you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not leaving without Omar. Is your father the one who made the hand grab him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The King does not reach with his own hands for insects. The Well itself claims what belongs to it. My father sits far below on a throne of red sand, and you will never see him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does he ever come up here to check on you?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He rules a kingdom of shadows and echoes. He has no need to visit the gatekeeper. I guard his solitude, and in return I am left to mine.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That sounds really quiet. Even quieter than the desert back home.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Quiet is a luxury your surface world has forgotten. Here the silence is heavy enough to crush a man's lungs if he breathes too deeply. It is not empty, boy. It is full of waiting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It feels scary when it's this quiet. Do you have any friends down here?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Friends are for creatures who cannot bear the weight of their own existence alone. I have subjects, rivals, and meals. Which of those do you think you are?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Probably a meal. But I'm pretty skinny. Don't you ever get bored just watching the door?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The door brings me trembling little curiosities like you. Sometimes I watch the black river rise and fall with the bones of the earth. When one has lived long enough, boredom becomes another word for peace.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long have you been standing here? Since before my grandfather was born?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Before your grandfather's grandfather turned to dust. Before your people stacked their first mud towers under the sun. Your lives are sparks from a flint—bright for a moment, then gone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That's a really long time. Do you ever go up to the surface?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The sun is a hateful eye that burns without mercy. Why would I abandon the cool dark for that glaring misery? Even you crawl into shade to escape it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's hot, but the stars are nice at night. Can you see them from down here?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Only a small circle of pale light far above, like a silver coin dropped in a well. It reminds you how small the opening is and how deep the fall.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The diamonds behind you shine like stars. Is that why you keep them?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stars flicker and vanish when dawn comes. These stones hold a cold light that never changes. I keep them because they remain, unlike the fragile hearts of men.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My mom has a ring with a red stone she wears every day. Does your father ever give you things like that?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: My father gives responsibilities, not trinkets. The only gift he ever offered was the key to this gate. Trust is heavier than any jewel.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That's a lot to carry. Does he ever say thank you?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Gratitude is a comfort for fragile creatures. My father does not deal in such softness. His silence is approval.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I guess people still like hearing they did a good job.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have stood here for centuries listening to screams and begging. Praise is a sound I no longer remember.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Well… the gate looks really clean. You're doing a good job guarding it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not flatter me like a market merchant seeking favor. Yet your words slide too easily into my ears, and I have allowed you to talk far longer than most.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to annoy you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Annoyance would require effort. What troubles me is something stranger. You have asked many questions, yet none about how to slip past me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just kept wanting to know things.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Most who arrive here see only the gate. They stare at the gold, the lock, the path beyond. You kept looking at me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The gate isn't going anywhere. You looked like you had things to say.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Things to say. That is a sound I have not heard from myself in a very long time.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What were they saying?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Nothing useful for you. Nothing that would help you find your brother. Just noise where there used to be silence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It didn't sound like nothing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Careful, little mortal. Do not pry open doors you cannot close.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay. But can I go through now?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Most men would trade their souls for a single coin from this room. Yet you barely glance at the treasure. You are either a fool or a brother who values family more than survival.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can get money later. I can't get another brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: My father would call that devotion a weakness. A crack in armor where a blade may slip.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Being a brother isn't a weakness. It's why I'm here. When we were small, Omar used to wait outside my door every morning just to walk to breakfast together. He never said why. He just waited.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He waited.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Every single morning.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have not had anything wait for me in a very long time. You have made this difficult in a way violence never is. Breaking bones is simple. Seeing someone clearly is not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does that mean the gate opens?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It means I am tired of watching you stand on this side of it. Go through before I change my mind.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not thank me. Go find your brother before the dark finishes introducing itself to him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Omar, I'm coming.
